photos.fun_fact: The Ghostface mask used in the film was an existing off-the-shelf Halloween costume mask that the production licensed, rather than one designed specifically for the movie.

photos.subject: Eiffel Tower, Paris
photos.fun_fact: Built in 1889, it was the world's tallest structure for 41 years until the Chrysler Building surpassed it.

photos.subject: Bahrain World Trade Center, Manama
photos.fun_fact: Its sail-shaped towers funnel wind to three turbines that supply up to 15% of the building's electricity.

photos.subject: Burj Al Arab, Dubai
photos.fun_fact: Its site was called 'Chicago Beach,' named after the Chicago Bridge and Iron Company that once welded oil tanks there.

photos.subject: Chrysler Building, New York
photos.fun_fact: Its spire was secretly assembled inside the building, then raised in just 90 minutes to beat a rival for tallest title.

photos.subject: Minerva Radio 505
photos.fun_fact: Minerva was an Austrian radio brand with production also based in Paris and Milan, and the 505 series were tube-based superheterodyne sets typical of the vacuum-tube radios sold across Europe in the early 1950s.

photos.subject: AC/DC - Back in Black
photos.fun_fact: The album was recorded as a tribute to former singer Bon Scott, who had died earlier that year, and its all-black cover was chosen as a symbol of mourning.

photos.subject: Oriental Pearl Tower, Shanghai
photos.fun_fact: The tower's distinctive design links eleven spheres of varying sizes, intended by its architects to evoke pearls being dropped onto a jade plate, referencing a famous line of Chinese poetry.

photos.subject: Amadeus
photos.fun_fact: Tom Hulce learned to convincingly mimic piano and conducting technique for the role of Mozart, and the production used real 18th-century candlelit palaces in Prague in place of Vienna, which had changed too much.

photos.subject: Apple Newton MessagePad
photos.fun_fact: The Newton popularized the term 'personal digital assistant,' but its handwriting recognition software was so unreliable at launch that it became a running joke, famously parodied on The Simpsons.

photos.subject: 2001: A Space Odyssey
photos.fun_fact: Stanley Kubrick worked with NASA consultants and futurists to design technology for the film, and its depiction of tablet-like devices and video calls is often cited as eerily predictive.

photos.subject: Banksy's Flower Thrower (Love is in the Air)
photos.fun_fact: The stencil depicts a masked rioter hurling a bouquet instead of a weapon and was originally painted on a wall in Bethlehem, becoming one of Banksy's most reproduced images.

photos.subject: Argo
photos.fun_fact: The film dramatizes a real 1980 CIA operation that used a fake Hollywood science-fiction film as cover to extract six American diplomats from Iran, and much of that cover story was genuinely produced for the ruse.

question: How many people can it hold?

photos.subject: Aviva Stadium, Dublin
photos.fun_fact: Built on the site of Lansdowne Road, which opened in 1872, making this one of the world's oldest continuously used sports grounds.

photos.subject: Pancho Arena, Felcsút
photos.fun_fact: Designed by architect Imre Makovecz, its organic wooden roof canopy is supported by tree-shaped pillars, giving the arena the feel of a forest glade rather than a football ground.

photos.subject: Signal Iduna Park, Dortmund
photos.fun_fact: Home to the famous 'Yellow Wall' (Südtribüne), Europe's largest free-standing terrace holding 24,454 standing fans on match day.

photos.subject: Qizhong Forest Sports City Arena, Shanghai
photos.fun_fact: Its retractable roof consists of eight steel 'petals' that open and close like a magnolia flower, Shanghai's official city flower.

photos.subject: Atari Lynx
photos.fun_fact: It was the first handheld game console with a full-color backlit LCD screen, beating Nintendo's monochrome Game Boy on visuals but suffering from a much shorter battery life.

photos.subject: A Clockwork Orange
photos.fun_fact: Stanley Kubrick personally withdrew the film from distribution in the United Kingdom in 1973 after it was blamed for copycat violence, and it wasn't legally shown there again until after his death in 1999.

photos.subject: Banksy's Girl with Balloon
photos.fun_fact: A print of this image partially shredded itself moments after selling at a Sotheby's auction in 2018 via a hidden mechanism Banksy had built into the frame years earlier.

photos.subject: Bambi
photos.fun_fact: Animators studied real deer at a small zoo set up on the studio lot, and the forest fire sequence was considered so intense that it was trimmed for younger audiences on some early releases.

photos.subject: Bell Dataphone (300 series)
photos.fun_fact: AT&T's Dataphone 300 series modem could send data at 300 bits per second over ordinary phone lines, laying groundwork for the encoding scheme still referred to today as 'Bell 103 modulation.'

photos.subject: Ben-Hur
photos.fun_fact: The galley sequence required building a full-scale Roman warship section on hydraulic rams in a studio tank, and Charlton Heston spent weeks training to row convincingly for the grueling slave scenes.

photos.subject: Black Sabbath - Paranoid
photos.fun_fact: The title track was written and recorded in about 25 minutes as filler because the album was running short, yet it became the band's biggest hit single.

photos.subject: Braveheart
photos.fun_fact: Mel Gibson directed and starred in the film, and thousands of Irish Army reservists were used as extras for the massive battle scenes since Scotland's own reserve force was too small.

photos.subject: Elizabeth Tower (Big Ben), Palace of Westminster, London
photos.fun_fact: Although the whole clock tower is popularly nicknamed 'Big Ben,' that name officially refers only to the Great Bell housed inside it, not the tower itself.

photos.subject: Sidu River Bridge, China
photos.fun_fact: When it opened in 2009, its deck sat 496 meters above the river, briefly making it the highest bridge in the world, and workers used a rocket to fire the first cable across the canyon.

photos.subject: Transamerica Pyramid, San Francisco
photos.fun_fact: Its distinctive pyramid shape was chosen partly to let more daylight reach the streets below than a conventional boxy skyscraper of the same size would allow, and it was the tallest building in San Francisco for decades.

photos.subject: Ulmer Münster, Germany
photos.fun_fact: It took over 500 years to finish, with a massive 300-year break in construction during the middle centuries before finally being completed in 1890.

photos.subject: ...Baby One More Time, Britney Spears
photos.fun_fact: The album's title track was originally offered to and turned down by other pop acts including TLC before Britney Spears recorded it, launching her career.

photos.subject: Casablanca
photos.fun_fact: The film's screenplay was still being rewritten during production, and the cast reportedly didn't know until near the end of shooting which man Ilsa would ultimately leave with.

photos.subject: Bruce Springsteen - Born in the U.S.A.
photos.fun_fact: Despite its anthemic sound, the title track is a bitter song about a disillusioned Vietnam veteran, a nuance often missed by politicians who have tried to use it as a campaign song.

photos.subject: Coexist logo
photos.fun_fact: Polish graphic designer Piotr Mlodozeniec created the design, spelling the word with religious symbols, as an entry for an art competition on the theme of coexistence in Jerusalem.

photos.subject: Curiosity Rover
photos.fun_fact: The rover's landing used an unprecedented 'sky crane' maneuver that lowered it to the Martian surface on cables from a hovering rocket stage, a sequence NASA engineers nicknamed 'seven minutes of terror.'

photos.subject: Das Boot
photos.fun_fact: The production built a full-scale, functional replica of a German U-boat, and director Wolfgang Petersen shot much of the claustrophobic interior action with handheld cameras to heighten the tension.

photos.subject: Die Hard
photos.fun_fact: Bruce Willis reportedly wasn't the studio's first choice, and the film was based on a novel that was itself a sequel to an earlier book, only loosely connected to the movie's plot.

photos.subject: Douglas DC-3
photos.fun_fact: The rugged, twin-engine airliner is credited with making passenger air travel profitable for the first time, and hundreds of surviving examples are still flying commercially today.

question: How many people can it hold?

photos.subject: Caesars Superdome, New Orleans
photos.fun_fact: Served as a shelter of last resort for thousands during Hurricane Katrina in 2005, sustaining significant damage to its roof during the storm.

photos.subject: Forsyth Barr Stadium, Dunedin
photos.fun_fact: The first stadium in the world with a natural grass pitch under a permanent fully enclosed roof, made from transparent ETFE panels.

photos.subject: Providence Park, Portland
photos.fun_fact: One of the oldest purpose-built soccer venues in the US, originally opened in 1926 and later expanded underground to add 4,000 seats below street level.

photos.subject: Tórsvøllur, Tórshavn
photos.fun_fact: Located on one of the most remote archipelagos in Europe, where matches can be interrupted by sudden ocean fog rolling in from the North Atlantic.

photos.subject: Leaning Tower of Pisa
photos.fun_fact: The tower began tilting even before construction was finished due to soft ground beneath its foundation, and engineers only stabilized its lean with major soil-correction work completed in 2001.

photos.subject: Dumb and Dumber
photos.fun_fact: Jim Carrey took a pay cut for the role, accepting a flat fee instead of his usual asking price, a decision that paid off handsomely once the film became a massive box-office hit.

photos.subject: IBM Selectric electric typewriter
photos.fun_fact: Instead of individual swinging type bars, the Selectric used a interchangeable spherical 'golf ball' typing element that moved across the page, letting users swap fonts in seconds.

photos.subject: Eminem - The Marshall Mathers LP
photos.fun_fact: The album became one of the fastest-selling solo albums in U.S. history at the time of its release and drew significant controversy in Congress over its explicit lyrics.

photos.subject: Everything Everywhere All at Once
photos.fun_fact: Michelle Yeoh trained extensively in martial arts and absurdist physical comedy for the film, which went on to sweep major categories at the Academy Awards, including Best Picture.

photos.subject: Ferrari F40
photos.fun_fact: It was the last Ferrari personally approved by company founder Enzo Ferrari before his death, and it was the first production car to break the 200 mph barrier.

photos.subject: Drake - Take Care
photos.fun_fact: The album's title track samples a Jamie xx remix of a Gil Scott-Heron song, and the record won the Grammy Award for Best Rap Album.

photos.subject: Fight Club
photos.fun_fact: The soap bar props used in the film were made with a small amount of real fat to give them an authentic, slightly translucent appearance.

photos.subject: Blue Mosque, Istanbul
photos.fun_fact: Its six minarets, the tallest reaching 64 meters, caused controversy when built since only the mosque in Mecca had that many at the time, so the sultan funded a seventh minaret there to resolve the dispute.

photos.subject: Duge Bridge, China
photos.fun_fact: The bridge's deck sits 565 meters above the Beipan River gorge, roughly the height of a 200-story building, and its design won engineering's Gustav Lindenthal Gold Medal, sometimes called the 'Nobel Prize of bridges.'

photos.subject: Mont-Saint-Michel Abbey, Normandy
photos.fun_fact: The gilded statue of the Archangel Michael crowning the spire is itself about 4.5 meters tall, and legend holds the archangel appeared in a dream instructing a local bishop to build the sanctuary.

photos.subject: Golden Gate Bridge, San Francisco
photos.fun_fact: When completed in 1937, its towers made it the tallest bridge in the world, and its distinctive 'International Orange' color was chosen partly because it stands out clearly in San Francisco's frequent fog.

photos.subject: Finding Nemo
photos.fun_fact: Pixar animators studied real fish anatomy and ocean footage extensively, then deliberately made some scientifically inaccurate choices, like Nemo's damaged fin, to serve the story.

photos.subject: Sony Micro TV 5-303
photos.fun_fact: At the time of its release it was the world's smallest and lightest television set, and Frank Sinatra was reportedly so impressed by a demo unit that Sony personally delivered one to him at Paramount Pictures.

photos.subject: Ford Model T
photos.fun_fact: Henry Ford's moving assembly line, introduced a few years after the car's debut, eventually cut the time to build one Model T from over 12 hours to about 93 minutes.

photos.subject: Florence Cathedral (Duomo)
photos.fun_fact: Its enormous dome, engineered by Filippo Brunelleschi, was built without a wooden supporting frame using an innovative herringbone brick pattern, and it remains the largest brick dome ever constructed.

photos.subject: Goodfellas
photos.fun_fact: The famous Copacabana tracking shot was filmed in a single unbroken take, following the actors through the kitchen and into the club to avoid a long line at the front entrance.

photos.subject: Good Will Hunting
photos.fun_fact: Matt Damon and Ben Affleck wrote the screenplay together as young actors, originally envisioning it as more of a thriller before reshaping it into the drama that won them an Academy Award.

photos.subject: Hooray for Boobies, Bloodhound Gang
photos.fun_fact: The album's biggest single, 'The Bad Touch,' became an unlikely worldwide hit despite, or perhaps because of, its irreverent lyrics about human mating rituals.

photos.subject: Hubble Space Telescope
photos.fun_fact: Shortly after launch, engineers discovered its primary mirror had a flaw just 1/50th the width of a human hair, which astronauts corrected in 1993 by installing corrective optics, essentially giving the telescope glasses.

question: How many people can it hold?

photos.subject: Docklands Stadium, Melbourne
photos.fun_fact: Features the first fully retractable roof in the Southern Hemisphere, which takes just eight minutes to open or close.

photos.subject: Principality Stadium, Cardiff
photos.fun_fact: Was the first stadium in the UK to have a fully retractable roof, and sits in the heart of the city center just minutes from the main train station.

photos.subject: Stadion Kantrida, Rijeka
photos.fun_fact: Built dramatically into a cliff face directly overlooking the Adriatic Sea, offering spectators views of both the match and the coastline.

photos.subject: Toyota Stadium, Toyota City
photos.fun_fact: The city itself was renamed from Koromo to Toyota in 1959 after the car manufacturer, making this one of the few stadiums named after both its sponsor and host city simultaneously.

photos.subject: Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade
photos.fun_fact: Sean Connery was cast as Indiana Jones's father despite being only twelve years older than Harrison Ford, and his ad-libbed comic timing reshaped much of the role during filming.

photos.subject: National Intelics solid-state radio
photos.fun_fact: Marketed under Panasonic's 'National' brand, the Intelics line was part of the wave of compact solid-state transistor radios that replaced bulkier vacuum-tube sets in the early 1970s.

photos.subject: Jurassic Park
photos.fun_fact: The film mixed then-groundbreaking CGI with practical animatronic dinosaurs built by Stan Winston's studio, and many of the close-up dinosaur shots are actually the physical puppets, not computer effects.

photos.subject: Ferrari Testarossa
photos.fun_fact: Its name means 'redhead' in Italian, referencing the red-painted cylinder heads of the engine, and its dramatic side strakes were designed to feed air to side-mounted radiators.

photos.subject: Kiss - Alive!
photos.fun_fact: The double live album was largely re-recorded and enhanced in the studio afterward, but it captured the band's theatrical stage show and became the breakthrough hit that launched their mainstream career.

photos.subject: Life Is Beautiful
photos.fun_fact: Roberto Benigni both directed and starred in the film, which blends comedy with the story of a father shielding his son from the horrors of a Nazi concentration camp, and it won three Academy Awards.

photos.subject: The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King
photos.fun_fact: The film swept all eleven Academy Awards it was nominated for, tying the record for the most Oscar wins for a single film.

photos.subject: Hitachi Magic Wand
photos.fun_fact: Hitachi originally marketed the corded device purely as a muscle and back massager, and it was later named one of Time magazine's most influential gadgets of all time.

photos.subject: Himeji Castle, Japan
photos.fun_fact: Despite standing for centuries through wars, earthquakes, and World War II bombing raids on the surrounding city, the castle keep itself has never actually been attacked.

photos.subject: Huajiang Canyon Bridge, China
photos.fun_fact: Opened in 2025, it became the first bridge in the world to break the 600-meter height barrier, surpassing the previous record holder, the Duge Bridge, by 60 meters.

photos.subject: Lake Palace, Udaipur
photos.fun_fact: Built entirely of white marble on a small island in Lake Pichola, the low, sprawling palace was designed to seem to float on the water, and it later served as a filming location for the James Bond film Octopussy.

photos.subject: Leaning Tower of Pisa, Italy
photos.fun_fact: The tower's tilt actually varies along its height because builders tried to compensate for the lean mid-construction by making upper stories slightly taller on the short side, giving the tower a subtle banana-like curve.

photos.subject: Magnavox Videomatic
photos.fun_fact: Videomatic was Magnavox's long-running line of automatic-tuning color television consoles, advertised for decades as offering hands-free brightness and contrast adjustment via an early photocell 'eye.'

photos.subject: Kill Bill: The Whole Bloody Affair
photos.fun_fact: This was a special one-time theatrical cut that combined both volumes of Kill Bill into a single film with restored footage, including the previously censored anime sequence in color.

photos.subject: Metallica - Master of Puppets
photos.fun_fact: It was the last album recorded with bassist Cliff Burton, who died in a tour bus accident shortly after its release, and it's widely regarded as one of the defining thrash metal records.

photos.subject: Metropolis
photos.fun_fact: The film's ambitious production nearly bankrupted its studio, and a nearly complete print thought lost for decades was rediscovered in a museum in Buenos Aires in 2008.

photos.subject: Motorola DynaTAC 8000X
photos.fun_fact: It was the first handheld commercial cell phone, weighed about two and a half pounds, offered roughly 30 minutes of talk time, and cost nearly $4,000 at launch.

photos.subject: Singin' in the Rain
photos.fun_fact: Gene Kelly performed the iconic title dance number while running a high fever, and the milk mixed into the rainwater on set was added to help it show up better on camera.

photos.subject: Nas - Illmatic
photos.fun_fact: Despite modest initial sales, the album is now widely regarded as one of the greatest hip-hop records ever made, built from productions by a rotating team of celebrated New York producers.

photos.subject: For a Few Dollars More
photos.fun_fact: It was the second film in Sergio Leone's 'Dollars Trilogy,' and its pocket watch motif inspired the famous extended standoff musical cues later used throughout the series.

question: How many people can it hold?

photos.subject: National Stadium, Kaohsiung
photos.fun_fact: Designed by Japanese architect Toyo Ito to resemble a dragon, its roof is covered with 8,844 solar panels that generate enough electricity to power the surrounding neighborhood.

photos.subject: San Siro, Milan
photos.fun_fact: Uniquely shared by fierce city rivals AC Milan and Inter Milan since 1947, with each club calling it home on alternating weekends.

photos.subject: Stadion Energa Gdańsk
photos.fun_fact: Built for Euro 2012, its amber-colored facade was inspired by the Baltic amber for which Gdańsk has been famous for centuries.

photos.subject: Strawberry Arena, Stockholm
photos.fun_fact: Its exterior is covered with 13,500 LED light panels that can display animations visible across the city skyline.

photos.subject: Nobody Likes Me, street art by I Heart
photos.fun_fact: Canadian street artist I Heart stenciled this piece of a boy shrieking at his phone in Vancouver, satirizing the anxiety of checking social media likes.

photos.subject: Ocean's Eleven
photos.fun_fact: Steven Soderbergh's star-studded cast reportedly all accepted lower-than-usual fees for the chance to work together, and the production was able to film inside real operating Las Vegas casinos including the Bellagio.

photos.subject: Osborne 1
photos.fun_fact: It was the first commercially successful portable computer, weighing about 24 pounds and bundled with thousands of dollars worth of software included in its price.

photos.subject: Parasite
photos.fun_fact: It became the first non-English-language film to win the Academy Award for Best Picture, and director Bong Joon-ho had a nearly full-scale replica of the wealthy family's house built specifically for filming.

photos.subject: Pet Shop Boys - Actually
photos.fun_fact: The album's artwork famously features Neil Tennant looking bored in every photo, a deadpan aesthetic the duo cultivated deliberately as part of their image.

photos.subject: Philips N1500 VCR
photos.fun_fact: It was the first videocassette recorder sold for home use, though its bulky cassettes could hold only about 30 to 60 minutes of recording time.

photos.subject: Pink Floyd - The Wall
photos.fun_fact: The album is a rock opera built around themes of isolation, and its accompanying stage shows famously involved building a literal wall of cardboard bricks across the stage during the performance.

photos.subject: Polaroid EE33
photos.fun_fact: It was a simple, low-cost instant camera aimed at casual snapshooters, using Polaroid's Type 88 pack film and an electric-eye exposure system for point-and-shoot simplicity.

photos.subject: Mike O'Callaghan-Pat Tillman Memorial Bridge, Nevada/Arizona
photos.fun_fact: It is the highest concrete arch bridge in the world, and its roadway was built roughly 1,500 feet downstream of Hoover Dam specifically so drivers wouldn't be tempted to gawk at the dam while driving.

photos.subject: Florence Cathedral (Duomo), Florence
photos.fun_fact: Filippo Brunelleschi engineered the dome without any wooden supporting scaffolding, inventing new construction machinery and a herringbone brick pattern to make it self-supporting as it rose.

photos.subject: Millau Viaduct, France
photos.fun_fact: Its tallest mast rises higher than the Eiffel Tower, making it the tallest bridge structure on Earth, even though its road deck itself sits somewhat lower above the Tarn River valley below.

photos.subject: Oriental Pearl Tower, Shanghai
photos.fun_fact: Its distinctive design links eleven spheres of different sizes along the structure, a concept its architects said was inspired by the classical Chinese poetic image of pearls dropping onto a jade plate.

photos.subject: Polaroid SX-70
photos.fun_fact: It was the first fully automatic, folding, single-lens reflex instant camera, ejecting self-developing photos that visibly developed in front of the photographer's eyes.

photos.subject: Prince - 1999
photos.fun_fact: The title track was released as a single ahead of Y2K anxieties and became an enduring anthem, re-charting decades later whenever the actual year 1999 or 2000 approached.

photos.subject: Pulsar calculator watch
photos.fun_fact: Pulsar's calculator watch let wearers punch in basic math using a tiny stylus stored in the watchband, and it was an expensive novelty status symbol of the mid-1970s digital watch boom.

photos.subject: Slumdog Millionaire
photos.fun_fact: Large portions of the film were shot on location in Mumbai's real slums with local child actors, and it went on to win eight Academy Awards including Best Picture.

photos.subject: Ramones - Ramones
photos.fun_fact: The band's debut album was recorded in about a week for roughly $6,400, and its stripped-down, fast, three-chord songs are widely credited with helping ignite the punk rock movement.

photos.subject: Rear Window
photos.fun_fact: Alfred Hitchcock shot almost the entire film from the confined point of view of a photographer with a broken leg, using a single, elaborately constructed courtyard set built on a soundstage.

photos.subject: Sampo solid-state television
photos.fun_fact: Taiwanese electronics maker Sampo built solid-state, transistorized televisions during the shift away from vacuum-tube sets in the 1960s and 1970s, later partnering with Sony and Sharp on manufacturing in Taiwan.

photos.subject: Saving Private Ryan
photos.fun_fact: The opening Omaha Beach sequence used veteran consultants and a stripped-down camera process to mimic the look of World War II combat newsreel footage, and it's still cited as one of the most realistic battle scenes ever filmed.

photos.subject: Schindler's List
photos.fun_fact: Steven Spielberg shot the film almost entirely in black and white and largely on location in Poland, including scenes filmed just outside the gates of the real Auschwitz.

photos.subject: Mont-Saint-Michel
photos.fun_fact: According to legend, the Archangel Michael appeared to a local bishop in a dream, instructing him to build a sanctuary on the rocky tidal island.

photos.subject: Memento
photos.fun_fact: Christopher Nolan structured the film in reverse chronological order to place the audience in the same short-term memory loss as its protagonist, so viewers piece the mystery together backwards.

photos.subject: Sony Discman D-50
photos.fun_fact: It was the first portable CD player ever sold, roughly the size of four stacked CD cases, and it helped kick off the format's shift from a home audio novelty to a mainstream product.

photos.subject: Star Wars: Episode VI - Return of the Jedi
photos.fun_fact: Practical effects and puppetry were used extensively for creatures like Jabba the Hutt, whose large animatronic body required a team of puppeteers to operate.

photos.subject: Sony Trinitron
photos.fun_fact: Sony's Trinitron used a single electron gun with three cathodes instead of the usual three separate guns, producing sharper, brighter images that earned the technology an Emmy Award in 1973.

photos.subject: The Intouchables
photos.fun_fact: The film is based on the real friendship between a wealthy quadriplegic man and his caregiver, and it became one of the highest-grossing non-English-language films ever released.

photos.subject: Himeji Castle
photos.fun_fact: Despite standing for centuries through wars, earthquakes, and World War II bombing raids on the surrounding city, the castle keep itself has never actually been attacked.

photos.subject: Star Wars: Episode IV - A New Hope
photos.fun_fact: Industrial Light & Magic was founded specifically to create the film's groundbreaking special effects, and it grew into one of the most influential visual effects studios in film history.

photos.subject: Atari 2600
photos.fun_fact: It was originally sold under the name Atari Video Computer System, and its swappable cartridges helped establish the idea that a single console could play many different games.

photos.subject: The Departed
photos.fun_fact: The film is a remake of the Hong Kong thriller Infernal Affairs, and it finally won Martin Scorsese his first competitive Academy Award for directing.

photos.subject: Sony Walkman Professional WM-D6C
photos.fun_fact: Prized by audio professionals and field recordists for its unusually high-fidelity cassette mechanism, this model remained in production for over two decades, far longer than most Walkman models.

photos.subject: The Great Escape
photos.fun_fact: The story is based on a real mass escape by Allied prisoners of war from a German camp, though the film compresses and dramatizes events, including adding Steve McQueen's famous motorcycle chase, which never happened in reality.

photos.subject: Nintendo Entertainment System
photos.fun_fact: To distance itself from the video game industry crash of 1983, Nintendo marketed the NES less as a game console and more as an 'entertainment system,' even including a robotic accessory called R.O.B.

photos.subject: The Lion King
photos.fun_fact: Animators studied real lion behavior at wildlife parks, and the film's story draws loose inspiration from both Hamlet and the Biblical story of Joseph.

photos.subject: Blue Mosque, Istanbul
photos.fun_fact: The mosque is officially named the Sultan Ahmed Mosque, and it earned its popular nickname from the tens of thousands of handmade blue Iznik tiles that decorate its interior.

photos.subject: The Rolling Stones - Sticky Fingers
photos.fun_fact: The original vinyl packaging featured a working zipper on a close-up photo of denim-clad jeans, a design by Andy Warhol that damaged album covers stacked in shipping crates.

photos.subject: The Shining
photos.fun_fact: Stanley Kubrick was notorious for demanding dozens of takes, and actress Shelley Duvall has said the exhausting shoot, which lasted over a year, took a significant physical and emotional toll on her.

photos.subject: The Silence of the Lambs
photos.fun_fact: It remains one of only three films to win all five major Academy Awards, including Best Picture, Director, Actor, Actress, and Screenplay.

photos.subject: The Sixth Sense
photos.fun_fact: The film's twist ending prompted a wave of repeat viewings in theaters, as audiences went back specifically to catch the subtle clues planted earlier in the story.

photos.subject: The Truman Show
photos.fun_fact: The fictional town of Seahaven was filmed in the real planned community of Seaside, Florida, whose deliberately idyllic architecture made it an ideal stand-in for a manufactured world.

photos.subject: The Who - Who's Next
photos.fun_fact: The album emerged from the ashes of Pete Townshend's abandoned multimedia rock opera project 'Lifehouse,' and its synthesizer-driven opening track became one of rock's most sampled recordings.

photos.subject: Michael Jackson - Thriller
photos.fun_fact: It remains the best-selling album of all time worldwide, and its accompanying music video, directed by John Landis, is often credited with transforming music videos into a serious art form.

photos.subject: Up
photos.fun_fact: The film's opening montage depicting a couple's life together is frequently cited as one of the most emotionally powerful sequences in animation history, told almost entirely without dialogue.

photos.subject: WALL-E
photos.fun_fact: The film's first act contains almost no dialogue, relying instead on sound design and physical animation to tell its story, an unusual choice for a major studio release.

photos.subject: The Wolf of Wall Street
photos.fun_fact: The film is based on the real memoir of stockbroker Jordan Belfort, and Leonardo DiCaprio trained extensively to perform the exaggerated physical comedy of the Quaalude scene himself.

photos.subject: Wright Flyer II
photos.fun_fact: Built as an improvement on the original 1903 Flyer, this aircraft made the first-ever complete circular flight by an airplane, piloted by Wilbur Wright at Huffman Prairie, Ohio.

photos.subject: Wu-Tang Clan - Enter the Wu-Tang (36 Chambers)
photos.fun_fact: The album was recorded on a shoestring budget in a Staten Island basement studio and is now widely regarded as one of the most influential hip-hop records ever made.

photos.subject: Star Wars: Episode V - The Empire Strikes Back
photos.fun_fact: The now-famous 'I am your father' line is frequently misquoted; Darth Vader's actual line in the film never includes the words 'Luke, I am your father.'

photos.subject: Full Metal Jacket
photos.fun_fact: R. Lee Ermey, a former Marine drill instructor hired as a technical advisor, improvised much of his character's dialogue and was cast in the role after Kubrick was impressed by his ad-libbing.

photos.subject: The Pianist
photos.fun_fact: Director Roman Polanski, himself a Holocaust survivor, drew on his own childhood memories of the Warsaw Ghetto to shape the film's depiction of survival.

photos.subject: Lake Palace, Udaipur
photos.fun_fact: Built from white marble on an island in Lake Pichola as a royal summer retreat, it was later converted into a luxury hotel and has appeared as a filming location in the James Bond film Octopussy.

photos.subject: Apple QuickTake 100
photos.fun_fact: Co-developed with Kodak, it was one of the first consumer digital cameras sold in the United States, storing only about eight full-resolution images at a time on its internal memory.

photos.subject: Rocky
photos.fun_fact: Sylvester Stallone wrote the script in roughly three days and refused to sell it unless he was cast as the lead, despite studios offering much more money for the script alone.

photos.subject: No. 1 Brownie, Model B
photos.fun_fact: Named after characters from a popular children's book series, the Brownie was designed to be so simple and cheap that Kodak could market photography directly to children.

photos.subject: Elizabeth Tower, Palace of Westminster
photos.fun_fact: Although widely nicknamed 'Big Ben,' that name technically refers only to the tower's Great Bell, not the clock tower itself.
